name: desire for sex
perceptions: The body or mind desires sexual contact.

guidance.description: Human beings are sexual creatures, but Western culture is pretty shy about about the subject. If this topic is causing you problems, consider researching it.

variations.name: biological desire for sex
variations.description: The purely biological desire for sexual contact is a small part of the story for most of us. If this is causing a problem, consider the guidance under the main section.

variations.name: validating desire for sex
variations.description: Being attractive enough to find a partner can fulfill a desire for social validation.
perceptions: being sexually active means you're not ugly

variations.name: peer pressure desire for sex
variations.description: Some may feel the need to be sexually active to stay in the graces of a social group.
perceptions: being sexually active means you're cool

commentaries.quote: Conflicting social norms can make any kind of sex complicated. It may help to understand where your own desire is coming from: social pressures, habits, escape, or biology.

There are many that consider sex to be a private matter that shouldn't be openly discussed in case it encourages young people. This is understandable, as the consequences can be significant. Not only is having a baby life changing, but you don't really want to think about your grandparents in that way.
It is clear that sexual desire is one of the — if not the — strongest of human needs. Typically, it takes up a huge portion of our time, emotional energy, and lives.
Our failure to understand the real and paradoxical nature of human mating is costly, both scientifically and socially.
commentaries.attribution: David M. Buss in 'The Evolution of Desire'
